description: Feature backlog - Product Owner owns priority

items.title: backlog show displays sprint history from archive for the item
items.intent: When an item has sprint runs in archive/sprints.jsonl, backlog show must display a Sprint history section listing each run: date, status, and attempts. Without this, sprint history is invisible — users must manually grep the archive file.
steps: In cmd_backlog_show in .aishore/lib/cmd-backlog-read.sh, after the existing jq output block, look up the item ID in $ARCHIVE_DIR/sprints.jsonl
Use jq to select all entries where .itemId == the queried ID, sorted by .date ascending, limited to 10 most recent
If matching entries exist, print a Sprint history: header followed by each entry formatted as: date  status  (attempts: N)
If no archive entries exist for the item, omit the section entirely — do not print an empty header

acceptanceCriteria.text: show exits 0 for item with no archive entries
acceptanceCriteria.verify: id=$(.aishore/aishore backlog add --json "{\"title\":\"tmp-show-test\",\"intent\":\"temp item to verify backlog show works without archive data\"}" 2>&1 | grep -o "FEAT-[0-9]*" | head -1) && .aishore/aishore backlog show "$id" && .aishore/aishore backlog rm "$id" --force

acceptanceCriteria.text: Sprint history section appears for item with archive entry
acceptanceCriteria.verify: id=$(.aishore/aishore backlog add --json "{\"title\":\"tmp-arch-test\",\"intent\":\"temp item to verify sprint archive section display\"}" 2>&1 | grep -o "FEAT-[0-9]*" | head -1) && printf "{\"date\":\"2026-04-14\",\"itemId\":\"%s\",\"status\":\"complete\",\"attempts\":1}\n" "$id" >> backlog/archive/sprints.jsonl && result=$(.aishore/aishore backlog show "$id" 2>&1) && .aishore/aishore backlog rm "$id" --force && echo "$result" | grep -q "Sprint history"

items.groomingNotes: Visibility gap: sprint history only in item failCount field, not the archive. Implementation: jq lookup in sprints.jsonl after existing show output. Verify uses ^Sprint history anchor to avoid false positives.

items.title: backlog show falls back to archive for done/cleaned items
items.intent: backlog show <ID> must succeed for any item aishore has ever tracked — active or archived. Running backlog show on a done item that was cleaned must display the item with an [archived] label rather than failing with item not found.
items.description: dal_find_item searches only the active BACKLOG_DIR files. Once aishore clean archives completed items, backlog show <ID> returns an error. Fix: after find_item fails in cmd_backlog_show, search archive/backlog_done.json and archive/bugs_done.json, display with an archived label, exit 0.
steps: In cmd_backlog_show in lib/cmd-backlog-read.sh, after find_item fails, search ARCHIVE_DIR/backlog_done.json and ARCHIVE_DIR/bugs_done.json for the item ID
Archive files store items as a JSON array at the top level. Use: jq -e --arg id ID .[] | select(.id == $id) on each archive file
If found in archive, print an [archived] header line then display the item with the existing jq display block
Return 0 so callers do not treat archived item display as a failure
Only error when the item is not found in any file — active backlog or archive

acceptanceCriteria.text: backlog show on an archived done item displays the item with archived label
backlog show on archived item exits 0
backlog show on an unknown ID still exits non-zero

items.groomingNotes: Well-specified. FEAT-094 confirmed in archive/backlog_done.json. Steps correctly target cmd_backlog_show after find_item fails. Archive files use JSON array — jq .[] | select(.id == $id) is correct. Verify commands use real archived item. Must priority, clear implementation path.

items.title: run batch session prints sprint summary table at end
items.intent: After any auto-mode run session completes, a sprint summary must print — one row per item attempted showing ID, pass/fail, and attempts — followed by totals and elapsed time. The operator must not have to scroll the full log to know the session outcome.
items.description: cmd_run exits after run_sprint_loop without printing a summary. In auto mode (run done / run p0 / run p1), the operator has no quick recap. The fix is to print a summary table at the end of cmd_run when auto_mode is true, using the sprint_items, COMPLETED_IDS, and FAILED_IDS state already tracked in the loop.
steps: After run_sprint_loop returns in cmd_run (aishore main script, cmd_run function), check if auto_mode is true
Print a Sprint Session Summary header using log_header
Print a table: ITEM | STATUS | ATTEMPTS for each item in sprint_items[], looking up pass/fail from COMPLETED_IDS and FAILED_IDS associative arrays
Print totals line: X complete, Y failed, Z skipped
Print elapsed time from batch_start to now in minutes

acceptanceCriteria.text: print_sprint_summary function exists in the codebase
Sprint Session Summary or equivalent header is printed at end of batch

items.groomingNotes: print_sprint_summary function already exists at line 2990 of .aishore/aishore — it currently prints totals only (passed/failed counts and a header). Developer must extend it to print a per-item table before the totals line. sprint_items[], COMPLETED_IDS, and FAILED_IDS are all in scope. Verify 1 (run done exits 0) should already pass. Verify 2 checks for Sprint.*Summary|Session.*Summary which does not match current Mission complete/ended headers — developer must add this header.

items.title: Sprint summary report as markdown artifact
items.intent: After a batch run completes, aishore must produce a shareable markdown sprint report showing every item shipped, pass/fail status, duration, lines changed, regression suite results, core health, and totals — so users have a viral proof artifact they can paste in Slack or commit to the repo.
items.description: The sprint report is the single highest-ROI feature for adoption. When run done or run N completes, drop a markdown file (e.g. .aishore/data/reports/sprint-YYYY-MM-DD.md) and print a summary to stdout. Include: item table (ID, title, status, duration, lines +/-), regression suite stats, core health, heal items generated, and totals. Format it to be impressive when pasted in Slack or viewed on GitHub.
steps: Create a report generation function that reads sprint archive data for the current batch
Build the markdown template with item table, regression stats, core health, and totals
Call the report generator at end of batch run (after all items processed)
Write report to .aishore/data/reports/ with date-stamped filename
Print a compact version to stdout as the batch completion message

acceptanceCriteria.text: Running a batch produces a markdown report in .aishore/data/reports/
Report contains item table with ID, title, status, duration, lines changed
Report contains regression suite summary
Compact summary printed to stdout at batch end

Reports go to .aishore/data/reports/ (directory does not yet exist — developer must create it). AC verify #1 combines run done + file existence check; verify #2 and #3 are real assertions (fallbacks removed). Verify #4 checks that the report path appears in run output. Developer must run run done after implementing to generate the first report before AC can pass.

items.title: 30-second demo project for instant first-run experience
items.intent: A new user must be able to run aishore init --demo and within 3 minutes see aishore pick an item, develop it, validate it, and merge it on a tiny demo project — so they experience the full sprint lifecycle before investing time configuring their own project.
items.description: Create a demo mode in init that scaffolds a tiny self-contained project (e.g. a CLI tool or utility script) with a pre-groomed 5-item backlog and a working PRODUCT.md. After scaffolding, automatically run 1-2 sprints so the user sees the full pipeline. The demo project should produce something visible and impressive. This is the adoption funnel — try before you buy.
steps: Add --demo flag to init command
Create demo project template: small utility with PRODUCT.md and 5 pre-groomed backlog items
Demo items should be small enough to complete in under 2 minutes each
After scaffolding, automatically trigger 1-2 sprint runs
Print a clear message showing what happened and how to use aishore on their own project

acceptanceCriteria.text: init --demo flag is accepted without error
Demo creates a PRODUCT.md and pre-populated backlog
Demo items are sprint-ready with intent, steps, and AC

items.groomingNotes: Steps refined: removed auto-run step (users run manually for better first-run UX). Three AC verifies: (1) help docs --demo flag, (2) init --demo -y creates PRODUCT.md and backlog in cwd using tmpdir isolation, (3) demo backlog has at least 1 sprint-ready item. Developer must ensure init --demo works from any directory (reads AISHORE_ROOT from env, writes to cwd). The AISHORE_BIN tmpdir pattern is the standard way to test init in isolation.

items.title: Composable quality gates via config
items.intent: Teams must be able to declare custom quality gate commands in config.yaml (pre-flight, post-develop, pre-merge phases) that run alongside built-in gates — so aishore adds intent gates and regression protection on top of existing CI checks rather than replacing them, making adoption additive.
items.description: Add a gates section to config.yaml where users can add custom shell commands at each pipeline phase: pre_flight (before dev starts), post_develop (after dev, before validation), pre_merge (after validation, before merge). Each gate has a name and command. Built-in gates (regression suite, maturity protocol, validator agent) remain; custom gates run alongside them. A failing custom gate blocks the pipeline just like a built-in gate.
steps: Define gates schema in config.yaml with pre_flight, post_develop, pre_merge phases
Parse gate definitions from config during sprint setup
Execute custom gates at each phase alongside built-in gates
Report gate results (name, pass/fail, output) in sprint log
Include custom gate results in sprint report

acceptanceCriteria.text: Custom gates can be defined in config.yaml under a gates section
A failing custom gate blocks the sprint pipeline
Gate results appear in sprint logs

items.groomingNotes: Steps now specify exact hook points: _run_preflight (after regression suite), post-developer-pass (before validation), post-validator-pass (before merge). Gate runner takes phase name and returns 1 on failure. Requires yq for config parsing — graceful no-op when yq absent or gates section missing. Not marking ready: needs scoping decision on whether yq is required (currently optional). AC verify #3 is true-deferred — integration test needs a real sprint run with a custom gate. Developer should manually test with a gates.pre_flight: [{name: smoke, command: false}] to confirm blocking behavior before signaling pass.

items.title: GitHub Action for CI/headless sprint execution
items.intent: Users must be able to run aishore in GitHub Actions on a schedule or trigger so that pushing a PRODUCT.md change or adding a backlog item causes sprints to execute in CI and open PRs automatically — enabling the overnight factory workflow where you wake up to shipped features.

Needs: Claude API key as secret, gh token for PR creation, headless mode (no interactive prompts). Pairs with --pr mode (FEAT-121) so CI runs produce PRs rather than auto-merging to main. Include a sample workflow yaml users can copy.

Create entrypoint script that sets up environment and runs aishore
Handle headless Claude Code execution (CLAUDE_CODE_HEADLESS or equivalent)
Create sample workflow file (.github/workflows/aishore.yml) users can copy
Document CI setup in README or dedicated CI doc

items.title: Agent-agnostic backend abstraction for developer and validator agents
items.intent: The orchestration layer must support pluggable AI backends (not just Claude Code) via a config-driven agent backend setting — so that users of Aider, Codex CLI, or other tools can adopt aishore for its quality model (intent gates, regression protection, core-first discipline) without switching their AI tool.

Define a backend interface: a command template that receives the prompt file and working directory, returns exit code and result.json. Add backend config to config.yaml. This is a design-now, ship-incrementally feature — the abstraction should be clean even if only claude-code is implemented initially.
steps: Define agent backend interface: input (prompt file, workdir, context), output (exit code, result.json)
Extract current Claude Code invocation into a backend module
Add agent.backend config to config.yaml with claude-code as default
Create backend dispatch function that routes to the configured backend
Document how to add a custom backend

Risk: touching the agent invocation path could break the sprint loop. Not marking ready: this is a significant refactor that should not block feature delivery. items.title: Regression checks fail when verify commands contain ANSI color codes
items.intent: Regression suite verify commands that grep output from aishore CLI commands must strip ANSI escape codes before matching — because the CLI always emits color codes to stdout, causing grep patterns to fail on otherwise-correct output, which blocks all sprints with false pre-flight failures.
items.description: Multiple regression checks failed because verify commands grep CLI output that contains ANSI escape codes (e.g. \x1b[0;36m). The regression runner should strip ANSI codes from verify command output before evaluation, or verify commands should be written to handle colored output. Root cause: CLI functions use log_info/log_warning which emit ANSI codes even when output is piped. Options: (1) strip ANSI in regression runner before eval, (2) detect non-TTY in log functions and suppress color, (3) both.

items.title: Circuit breaker wastes attempts when all items hit the same pre-flight failure
items.intent: When the regression suite pre-flight fails, the circuit breaker must detect that subsequent items will hit the same failure and stop immediately after the first pre-flight failure — instead of burning through 5 items on an identical regression failure, wasting time and incrementing fail counts on items that never got a chance to run.
items.description: During a run done session, the regression suite failed due to stale entries. The circuit breaker correctly stopped after 5 failures, but it burned through 4 additional items that all failed on the identical pre-flight check. It should detect that pre-flight failures are systemic (same failure across items) and stop after the first one, or at least after 2. The current circuit breaker only counts consecutive failures without distinguishing failure phase (pre-flight vs AC vs validation).

items.title: Chicken-and-egg: regression fix items cannot run because regressions block pre-flight
items.intent: When a backlog item exists specifically to fix the regression suite (like BUG-154), the orchestrator must allow it to bypass the pre-flight regression check — because requiring the regression suite to pass before running the item that fixes the regression suite creates an unresolvable deadlock that requires manual intervention.
items.description: BUG-154 was created to fix stale regression entries blocking pre-flight. But BUG-154 itself could not run because pre-flight (which runs the regression suite) failed. This is a fundamental design flaw: the system cannot self-heal regression suite issues. Options: (1) items tagged track:core or with specific keywords bypass pre-flight, (2) if an items intent/title references regression suite, skip regression pre-flight for that item, (3) add a --skip-preflight flag for manual override, (4) if pre-flight fails, auto-check if any queued item is specifically about fixing regressions.

items.title: Duplicate regression entries accumulate in regression.jsonl
items.intent: The regression archiver must deduplicate verify commands before appending to regression.jsonl — because BUG-150 had 3 identical entries (same verify command copied 3 times), and duplicate entries multiply pre-flight runtime and make stale entries harder to clean up.
items.description: BUG-150 Lock acquisition handles PID write failure had 3 copies of the same verify command in regression.jsonl. This suggests the archiver appends without checking for duplicates. Should deduplicate on (itemId + verify) before writing.

items.title: backlog check --all is too slow for use in regression suite
items.intent: backlog check --all must complete within 10 seconds for a typical backlog (20 items) — because the current implementation runs every verify command for every item sequentially, taking over 30 seconds for 16 items, which makes it unusable as a regression check and causes timeouts.
items.description: backlog check --all runs check_readiness_gates for each non-done item, which executes all AC verify commands. With 16 items, some having verify commands that themselves invoke aishore CLI commands, this takes over 30 seconds. The regression check for FEAT-103 was removed because it reliably timed out. Options: (1) parallelize verify command execution, (2) add --quick flag that skips verify commands, (3) cache recent verify results.

items.title: Stale feature branch blocks sprint start with fatal error
items.intent: When a feature branch already exists from a previous failed sprint, the orchestrator must handle it gracefully — either reusing the existing branch or deleting and recreating it — instead of hitting a fatal git error that wastes a sprint attempt.
items.description: FEAT-117 had a stale branch aishore/FEAT-117 from a previous crash. The run command hit fatal: a branch named aishore/FEAT-117 already exists when creating the worktree. The sprint continued but this is fragile. The crash recovery cleaned up the worktree directory but not the branch ref. The orchestrator should delete stale branches during crash recovery or handle the existing-branch case during worktree creation.

items.title: AC verify commands that create temp backlog items leak on failure
items.intent: When an AC verify command creates temporary backlog items (via backlog add) and the sprint fails before cleanup runs, the temp items persist in the backlog permanently — polluting the backlog with orphaned tmp-show-test and tmp-arch-test entries that require manual cleanup.
items.description: FEAT-112 verify commands use backlog add to create temp items, then backlog rm to clean up. When the developer agent fails or the verify command fails mid-execution, the rm never runs and temp items accumulate. After 2 runs with failures, 10 orphaned temp items appeared. Verify commands should not mutate backlog state, or should use a transaction pattern (create-test-cleanup in a trap).
